results.title: Seer Tech Product Intelligence - Oracle AI Database 26ai Demo
results.text:
High Tech product and manufacturing intelligence on one governed Oracle data platform.

This LiveStack demonstrates Oracle AI Database 26ai for High Tech across semiconductor manufacturing, fab operations, product lifecycle management, design-to-manufacturing handoff, electronics manufacturing, supplier risk, contract manufacturing, connected products, field quality, warranty analytics, service and support operations, order promising, and AI-assisted customer-commitment decisions.

NINE USE CASES, ONE HIGH TECH PRODUCT LIFECYCLE STORY

The demo follows a launch-at-risk scenario across semiconductor manufacturing, fab operations, product lifecycle management, design-to-manufacturing handoff, electronics manufacturing, supplier risk, demand volatility, channel inventory, customer commitments, field quality, warranty analytics, connected products, and service and support operations. Each scene uses the same governed Oracle AI Database 26ai foundation so the story stays connected from data load through AI-assisted action.

1
Data Foundation
Load one governed baseline for wafer starts, NPI programs, BOM revisions, supplier risk, fab capacity, order promising, channel inventory, field quality, warranty analytics, and connected-product signals.
2
High Tech Operations Command Center
See the design-to-manufacturing handoff risk before it becomes separate fab operations, electronics manufacturing, supplier, order, support, and quality escalations.
3
Product, Supply & Quality Signals
Explain the evidence across component shortages, demand volatility, yield improvement, engineering change orders, customer commitments, and service and support operations.
4
Product Lifecycle Event Graph
Trace how NPI milestones, product lifecycle management records, suppliers, contract manufacturing partners, BOM items, launch blockers, quality cases, and buyer commitments connect.
5
Supply Chain Resilience Map
Prioritize fabs, contract manufacturing sites, supplier lanes, availability centers, channel inventory pools, and order-promising decisions with Oracle Spatial evidence.
6
Customer Commitments
Open the order, allocation, connected-product, warranty, field-quality, and support records behind the launch and fulfillment commitment.
7
Yield, Capacity & Warranty Analytics
Predict wafer yield exposure, fab bottlenecks, component shortages, allocation risk, warranty escape rates, field quality exposure, and NPI launch readiness.
8
Ask High Tech Data
Ask the semiconductor manufacturing and electronics manufacturing story in plain language and let Oracle generate governed SQL over the live High Tech schema.
9
High Tech AI Agent Console
Convert findings into auditable actions for fab operations, product engineering, supply planning, contract manufacturing, quality, warranty, support, sales, and customer-commitment teams.

SCENE 2 - DETECT THE LAUNCH CONSTRAINT
Spot the product-launch risk before it fragments across teams.

The command center turns a constrained AI accelerator launch into one operating view: fab utilization, wafer-start plans, yield risk, supplier shortage exposure, design-to-manufacturing handoff readiness, channel inventory, contract manufacturing capacity, customer commitments, order-promising pressure, connected-product signals, field quality, warranty exposure, and support backlog surface together.

2

3

Use the dashboard as the handoff into signals, graph, map, analytics, Ask Data, and agents.

How the launch constraint is detected

Products are flagged when demand signals accelerate while supply flexibility tightens. The same inputs shown below are combined into a transparent 0–100 Constraint Risk score; higher scores indicate greater launch exposure.

Demand signal pressure · 80%
45% average virality, up to 20% signal concentration, and up to 15% matched-record volume.
Capacity pressure · 15%
Recent requested units compared with available units across the product network.
Supply flexibility · 5%
Added exposure when only one or two supply sites have units available for allocation.

SCENE 4 - TRACE THE PRODUCT LIFECYCLE PATH
Connect products, suppliers, BOMs, launch blockers, and commitments.

The graph scene shows how NPI records, product portfolios, developer and ecosystem signals, supplier constraints, component shortages, engineering change orders, bill of materials dependencies, contract manufacturing partners, capacity centers, field quality cases, warranty analytics, service operations, and customer commitments interact as one product lifecycle event graph.

1

Select a product, supplier, blocker, buyer, architecture, quality case, or commitment node.

2

Increase graph depth to expose multi-hop supplier, BOM, and mitigation relationships.

3

Use pathway findings to decide which launch or customer milestone needs attention first.

How risk scores and hops guide the decision

This demo keeps the scoring transparent. Higher values mean the selected product path is more likely to affect launch readiness or a customer commitment.

Stored case or node risk
The seeded 0–100 urgency score attached to the product signal evidence.
Derived pathway risk
Deep-path findings use 72 plus the number of entities found at three or more hops, capped at 99. Relationship hot spots use 60 plus five points per repeated relationship, capped at 100.
Why hops matter
A hop is one connected lifecycle step. More hops reveal longer dependency chains and more places where supplier, fab, quality, or allocation delays can propagate.

Explore multi-hop product lifecycle paths with Oracle Property Graph and SQL property graph queries across bill of materials, supplier risk, fab capacity, field quality, warranty, and customer commitments.

Partners With - Partner engineering, contract manufacturing, or supplier risk relationships support mitigation.
Routes to Capacity Center - Portfolio demand is routed to a fab, contract manufacturing site, or product availability center.
Supplied By - A bill of materials component, substrate material, memory stack, or product dependency is supplied by a supplier or supplier site.

Reviewed by Change Review Board - An engineering change order, new product introduction, or product lifecycle decision is reviewed by a change review board.

Correlates with Field Quality - A signal, telemetry pattern, or field incident correlates with field quality exposure.
